notice: Known consent-management-platform fingerprints and control selectors. A fingerprint match resolves controls directly and takes precedence over text scoring, because CMP vendors ship stable element ids while button labels vary by site, language, and configuration. Selectors are maintained heuristics: verify against the live DOM when a run reports a fingerprint match but a failed click, and treat an unrecognised CMP as the normal case rather than an error. Adding an entry here never changes how a finding is classified; it only makes the denial and accept paths reachable.

cmps.name: HubSpot cookie banner
cmps.notes: Element ids carry an 'eu' prefix for historical reasons; the banner is served to every visitor regardless of region. Buttons are labelled plainly 'Accept' and 'Decline', which is exactly the bare-label case that text scoring penalises. 'save' is deliberately empty: the simple banner has no separate save control, and mapping it to the confirmation button would turn a settings-path denial into an acceptance.

cmps.name: OneTrust
cmps.notes: A reject control is only rendered when the site enables it; absence of #onetrust-reject-all-handler is itself a reportable UI observation, not a detection failure.

cmps.name: Cookiebot (Usercentrics)
cmps.notes: Cookiebot is now owned by Usercentrics but ships a distinct DOM; keep both entries. #CybotCookiebotDialogBodyLevelButtonPreferences was removed from settings 2026-08-22: live capture showed it is a role=switch category-toggle checkbox, not a settings launcher - clicking it during execute_denial's settings step would have flipped a consent category instead of opening the preference panel.

cmps.name: Usercentrics CMP
cmps.notes: Renders inside a shadow root under #usercentrics-root; control collection must pierce shadow DOM or nothing will be found.

cmps.name: Sourcepoint
cmps.notes: Renders in a cross-origin iframe; Playwright frame traversal handles this, but the control will never appear in the main frame.

cmps.name: Didomi
cmps.notes: The generic preferences-layer button class is not used for 'save' because it also matches Didomi's agree control; 'save' resolved to the real #btn-toggle-save id 2026-08-22 after live capture, replacing an aria-label substring match that failed to localize (French 'Enregistrer'). The former accept fallback `button.didomi-components-button--color[aria-label*='Agree' i]` was removed the same day: 'Disagree' contains 'agree' as a substring, so it matched both the agree AND disagree buttons - a live regression, not a hypothetical one. `.didomi-continue-without-agreeing[role='button']` covers deployments (e.g. Chantelle) that ship no disagree button at all, only a 'continue without agreeing' link.

cmps.name: TrustArc
cmps.notes: The preference manager opens in an iframe from consent.trustarc.com. Verified 2026-08-22 against trustarc.com's own site: container/accept/reject/settings selectors are all correct and both accept ('Accept All') and reject ('Reject Optional') are directly visible at the first layer, no settings detour needed. The iframe-based preference manager was NOT observed on this lightweight marketing-site deployment - clicking 'Manage Settings' produced no consent.trustarc.com iframe here, which is consistent with the enterprise SaaS embed this note describes simply not being how TrustArc's own site is configured, not with the note being wrong. Not re-verified against an enterprise deployment that actually uses it.

cmps.name: Osano
cmps.notes: `.osano-cm-button--type_save` removed 2026-08-22: not observed on a live save control, which carries only `.osano-cm-save`. accept/reject selectors are retained as unverified compatibility fallbacks - all three sites checked served US-region configurations exposing only Manage Preferences (and one exposing only Close), so accept/deny-all controls were never observed rendered, not confirmed absent.

cmps.name: Termly
cmps.notes: `[data-tid='banner-preferences']` replaced with `[data-focus-id='preferences-button']` 2026-08-22: the current runtime's settings button carries the latter, not the former. `save` emptied to match: three live deployments each opened a preference modal offering only Decline All / Allow All, with no save control at all - an empty list here is accurate, not a gap, and is what routes this CMP through UNSAVED_PREFERENCE_STATUS if toggles are ever operated without one.

cmps.name: CookieYes
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against two live deployments, because CookieYes ships two mutually exclusive first-layer templates and only one of them is present in the DOM on any given site. GDPR/opt-in template captured on https://www.webyes.com: every selector in this entry matched real markup. `.cky-btn-accept`, `.cky-btn-reject` and `.cky-btn-customize` are the three first-layer controls under `.cky-notice-btn-wrapper`, and `save` (`.cky-btn-preferences`, aria-label 'Save My Preferences') sits in the preference-centre footer `.cky-prefrence-btn-wrapper` - the vendor's own misspelling - and is hidden until `.cky-btn-customize` adds `cky-modal-open` to `.cky-modal`. Driving the real settings -> save path with the default toggles (ckySwitchfunctional, ckySwitchanalytics, ckySwitchperformance, ckySwitchadvertisement, ckySwitchother, all off) wrote a genuine denial: `cookieyes-consent=...,consent:yes,action:yes,necessary:yes,functional:no,analytics:no,performance:no,advertisement:no,other:no`, so `.cky-btn-preferences` is a save-current-toggles control and not a disguised accept. `.cky-btn-accept` and `.cky-btn-reject` each match two elements (first layer plus preference-centre footer), but both members of each pair are controls of that same kind and _locate_by_selectors skips invisible candidates, so the duplication is harmless. CCPA/opt-out template captured on https://www.cookieyes.com (CookieYes' own site): the fingerprint matches - `.cky-consent-container` and `.cky-modal` are both present - but all four control selectors match nothing whatsoever, so a run against a CCPA deployment fingerprints as CookieYes and then reports cmp_table_miss on every kind. The real controls there are `.cky-btn-do-not-sell` (aria-label 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information', confirmed live to be a panel launcher rather than a reject: clicking it adds `cky-modal-open` and writes no cookie) and, inside that panel, `.cky-btn-confirm` (aria-label 'Save My Preferences') next to `.cky-btn-cancel` and the `#ckyCCPAOptOut` checkbox. They are deliberately NOT added to this entry: find_control's reject scoring already refuses to substitute a sale/share opt-out for a cookie denial ('a separate statutory mechanism'), and the CMP-table path runs before that scoring and bypasses the guard entirely, so listing `.cky-btn-do-not-sell` under `settings` would let execute_denial drive a CCPA opt-out and report it as a completed denial. cmp_table_miss is the correct outcome on that template. Recorded here too because it changes how `consent_storage` reads: completing the opt-out on cookieyes.com set `consent:yes,action:yes` while leaving `functional:yes,analytics:yes,performance:yes,advertisement:yes` untouched, so on a CCPA deployment the category flags inside `cookieyes-consent` do not express the opt-out and must not be read as consent.

cmps.name: Iubenda
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-23 against https://www.tannico.it, a live Iubenda customer deployment - iubenda.com's own site runs no CMP of its own (checked first: no #iubenda-cs-banner, no iubenda script host, no consent popup at all on https://www.iubenda.com). container/accept/settings/fingerprint/script_hosts/consent_storage all matched the real markup exactly, including the '_iub_cs-848639' cookie the consent_storage prefix targets. `reject` needed a second control, not a replacement: tannico.it renders no `.iubenda-cs-reject-btn`, checked both before and after opening the settings panel, but that is a per-site config toggle, not an absent control. The live runtime config on tannico.it reports `_iub.cs.options.banner.rejectButtonDisplay: false` (with `rejectButtonCaption: "Rifiuta"`), and the actual CMP bundle the site loads (`cdn.iubenda.com/cookie_solution/iubenda_cs/1.104.3/core-it.js`) renders `.iubenda-cs-reject-btn` precisely when that flag is true, wired to a dedicated `onRejectButtonClick` handler and its own CSS rule keyed off `rejectButtonColor`. So `.iubenda-cs-reject-btn` is the genuine one-click first-layer reject-all on any Iubenda deployment that enables it, and is kept in the table ahead of the fallback as a real-but-not-observed-on-this-capture control rather than deleted. The fallback, `.iubenda-cs-cwa-button` ('Continua senza accettare' / 'Continue without accepting'), is the same dismiss-without-agreeing shape already documented on the Didomi entry, and is what tannico.it itself renders since its reject button is disabled. Clicking it removes the banner and writes `_iub_cs-<id>` with every non-necessary purpose false, a complete one-click denial, confirmed live. `save` was also wrong: `.iub-cmp-save-btn` does not exist either; the real settings-panel save control is `#iubFooterBtn` ('Salva e continua'), an id with no distinguishing class of its own. The settings panel also exposes a `.purposes-btn-reject` ('Rifiuta tutto') bulk-toggle button, deliberately left out of `reject`: live testing showed clicking it alone only unchecks the optional-purpose checkboxes and writes no cookie and does not close the panel - `#iubFooterBtn` still has to be clicked afterward to commit, confirmed by clicking both in sequence and observing the cookie only appear after the second click. Including it in `reject` would have made execute_denial report `second_layer_reject_clicked` for a click that saved nothing, the same false-positive shape the Cookiebot preferences-checkbox bug was. Its toggle effect is instead reached through the existing settings -> toggle -> save fallback via the corrected `save` selector.

cmps.name: Quantcast Choice
cmps.notes: Quantcast relies on mode attributes rather than stable ids; positional fallbacks here are deliberately last-resort and should be confirmed against a screenshot. 'save' is empty because the primary-mode button in the preferences layer is the agree control, so mapping it would convert a denial into an acceptance. Partially checked 2026-08-22 against quantcast.com from a US browser: the `.qc-cmp2-container` fingerprint matched, but `#qc-cmp2-ui` did not, and the rendered UI was the CCPA `qc-cmp2-usp` opt-out modal (a single mode='primary' 'CONFIRM' button, no mode='secondary' at all) rather than the EU consent summary layer these accept/reject selectors target - the same US-region limitation the 2026-08-22 research pass hit on Osano. The mode='primary'/'secondary' accept/reject selectors remain unverified rather than disproved; do not fixture them from this capture.

cmps.name: Complianz (WordPress)
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-23 against two live deployments: complianz.io itself (dogfooding - both an 'optin' and a region-detected 'optout' template are templated into the DOM at once, only one shown per visitor's detected region) and wpcodetips.com, a real customer site on the default first-layer 'banner-1 banner-a optin' template. `container`, `accept` ('.cmplz-btn.cmplz-accept'), `reject` ('.cmplz-btn.cmplz-deny'), `save` ('.cmplz-btn.cmplz-save-preferences', hidden until the panel opens), and `consent_storage` all matched real markup exactly on both captures; clicking Deny on wpcodetips.com wrote real `cmplz_marketing=deny; cmplz_statistics=deny; cmplz_preferences=deny` cookies. `settings` was wrong: the real, functioning first-layer settings launcher on both captures is `<button class="cmplz-btn cmplz-view-preferences">` (confirmed live - clicking it adds `cmplz-categories-visible` to the banner and reveals 4 category toggles plus Save). The old `.cmplz-manage-options` selector matches two elements on real markup, neither of them that launcher: a permanently-hidden (w=0,h=0) footer text link `<a class="cmplz-link cmplz-manage-options cookie-statement" href=".../#cmplz-manage-consent-container">` that navigates to a different page rather than opening the panel in place, and an equally-hidden TCF-only variant. On both live captures this made `settings` resolve to nothing (cmp_table_miss) despite a real, visible, working launcher sitting right next to it under a different class.

cmps.name: Borlabs Cookie (WordPress)
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against https://borlabs.io (Borlabs' own site, plugin 3.4.2.2). This entry was written for Borlabs 2.x and every one of its selectors is a 2.x selector; on 3.x the plugin was rewritten as a Vue app and all six `[data-cookie-*]` attribute selectors - accept-all, refuse, back, individual, accept - matched nothing at all. The fingerprint still holds: `#BorlabsCookieBox` and `#BorlabsCookieWidget` are both present on 3.x, but `#BorlabsCookieBox` is an empty `data-v-app` mount point until a dialog is opened, so an entry that fingerprints fine can still resolve no controls whatsoever. The real 3.x controls, captured from the rendered dialog, are `.brlbs-btn-accept-all` ('Accept all'), `.brlbs-btn-accept-only-essential` ('Accept only essential cookies'), `.brlbs-btn-save` / `#CookieBoxSaveButton` ('Save'), `.brlbs-cmpnt-btn-selection` ('Select all' / 'Deselect all') and the persistent widget `.brlbs-cmpnt-widget` (aria-label 'Open Privacy Preferences Dialog', confirmed live to render the dialog into `#BorlabsCookieBox`). Those were added alongside the 2.x selectors rather than replacing them, so both generations resolve. The defect this capture found is `#CookieBoxSaveButton`, which was listed under `accept`. It is not an accept control: live on 3.x it is the button labelled 'Save', carrying `.brlbs-btn-save`, and its own id says so. Listing it under `accept` meant execute_accept on a Borlabs site would click Save - persisting whatever the default, mostly-denied selection happened to be - and report that as an acceptance, which understates what a real acceptance transmits and quietly corrupts the accept-vs-denial comparison the whole run exists to make. It was moved to `save`, where it belongs. Note this is the inverse of the usual hazard and test_cmp_table_integrity cannot catch it: the collision is semantic, and `save`'s `[data-cookie-accept]` and `accept`'s `[data-cookie-accept-all]` are textually different selectors, so nothing structural was ever going to flag it. `consent_storage` was widened. Clicking 'Accept only essential cookies' wrote two cookies, not one: `borlabs-cookie` (the consent record, `{'consents':{'essential':[...]},'domainPath':'.borlabs.io/',...}`) and `borlabs-cookie-gcs`, which carries the Google Consent Mode signals `{'ad_storage':'denied','ad_user_data':'denied','ad_personalization':'denied','analytics_storage':'denied'}`. The list held only the exact key `borlabs-cookie`, so the gcs cookie - the one that actually states the per-purpose denial - was not matched at all. A `borlabs-cookie-` prefix rule now covers it and any other suffixed sibling. Not verified, and left alone rather than guessed at: the 2.x `[data-cookie-*]` selectors, since no 2.x deployment was found to capture; and the in-banner 3.x settings control, because borlabs.io served this visitor no first-layer banner at all (the dialog was reachable only through the widget). `[data-cookie-back]` under `reject` is recorded here as doubtful on its face - a 'Back' control is dialog navigation, not a refusal - but it is left in place because it is unverified rather than known-wrong, and a reject selector that matches nothing cannot mis-click.

cmps.name: CookieLawInfo / GDPR Cookie Consent (WordPress)
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against three live deployments spanning both plugin lineages, plus the plugin's own cookie-law-info-public.js: https://onestiproducts.io (webtoffee-gdpr-cookie-consent 2.3.4, the only one of the three with a reject button enabled), https://wcrp-cmip.org/cookie-policy/ (same plugin, 2.3.9) and https://digitalinclusionkit.org (cookie-law-info 3.4.2 legacy path). `reject` was broken and is the reason this pass was worth taking. On onestiproducts.io the real, visible control is `Reject All` - so the id selector `#cookie_action_close_header_reject` matched nothing (the id is `wt-cli-reject-btn`) and `.cli-reject-btn` matched nothing either, on any of the three captures or anywhere in the plugin source. Both of this entry's reject selectors missed a rendered reject button that was sitting right there. The class form `.cookie_action_close_header_reject` was added and is what the plugin itself binds to (`this.reject_link = jQuery('.cookie_action_close_header_reject')`). The two dead selectors are left in place as inert fallbacks - a reject selector that matches nothing cannot mis-click anything - but `.cli-reject-btn` in particular is recorded here as unverified so a later pass does not assume it was checked. `accept` had the same id-versus-class confusion but got away with it: the id `#cookie_action_close_header` is real on 3.4.2 and absent on both 2.3.x captures (where the id is `wt-cli-accept-btn`), while the class `cookie_action_close_header` is present on all three, so it was added alongside. `.cli_action_button` on its own is NOT usable for accept - both the accept and the reject button carry it - which is exactly why the existing `[data-cli_action='accept']` qualifier is there; leave it. `settings` resolves everywhere via `.cli_settings_button`; `#cookie_action_settings` matched nothing on any capture and appears nowhere in the plugin source. `save` deserves the most attention and survived it. `.cli_setting_save_button` resolves to `Save & Accept` - labelled 'Save & Accept', carrying an accept-flavoured class and literally `data-cli-action='accept'`. It is nonetheless a genuine save, confirmed two ways. In the source the click handler only calls `enableAllCookies()` when the action is `accept_all`, which this is not; it then calls `accept_close()`, which writes the per-category cookies from the live checkbox states via `generate_user_preference_cookie()`. Live on onestiproducts.io, where `checkbox-analytics` ships pre-ticked, unticking analytics and clicking Save & Accept wrote `cookielawinfo-checkbox-analytics=no` and `CookieLawInfoConsent=eyJ2ZXIiOiIxIiwibmVjZXNzYXJ5IjoidHJ1ZSIsImFuYWx5dGljcyI6ImZhbHNlIn0=` (base64 for `{'ver':'1','necessary':'true','analytics':'false'}`). The toggles are honoured; the label lies. Do not 'fix' this by removing the selector. One trap in the same observation: `accept_close()` sets `viewed_cookie_policy='yes'` unconditionally, so that denial also left `viewed_cookie_policy=yes` behind. `viewed_cookie_policy` is in this entry's `consent_storage`, and read on its own it says 'yes' for an acceptance and for a settings-path denial alike - only the per-category keys separate them. `consent_storage` was widened accordingly. It previously listed only `cookielawinfo-checkbox-necessary`, which is the one category that is always yes and therefore the least informative; the live captures carry `cookielawinfo-checkbox-` cookies for necessary, functional, performance, analytics, advertisement and others, so that is now a `-` prefix rule (consent_key_matches supports one) and the five keys that actually record the decision stop being missed. `cli_user_preference` was added too: it is written by the same code path and was observed live as `en-cli-yes-checkbox-necessary-yes-checkbox-analytics-no`.

cmps.name: Klaro
cmps.notes: '.cm-btn-success' is Klaro's accept-all control and is deliberately excluded from 'save', so a settings-path denial cannot end in an acceptance.

cmps.name: Axeptio
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-22 against https://axept.io (Axeptio's own site). Live DOM: `#axeptio_overlay` is a light-DOM mount point whose only child is an open shadow-root host; the real controls live inside that shadow root as `#axeptio_btn_dismiss` (aria-label 'Close without accepting cookies', text 'No, thanks'), `#axeptio_btn_configure` (aria-label 'I choose the cookies to configure', text 'I want to choose'), and `#axeptio_btn_acceptAll` (aria-label 'Accept all cookies', text 'Ok for me'). The accept fallback `button[aria-label*='Accept' i]` was a live bug, not a hypothetical one, confirmed by querying the real shadow root: 'accepting' contains 'Accept' as a substring, so the selector matched three real buttons - #axeptio_btn_dismiss, #axeptio_btn_acceptAll, and the persistent widget's #axeptio_main_button - and DOM-order/`.first` resolution returned #axeptio_btn_dismiss (the reject-side control) ahead of the real accept button, mirroring the Didomi 'agree'/'disagree' collision exactly. Removed; `#axeptio_btn_acceptAll` alone is Axeptio's stable element id and is sufficient on its own. The existing reject fallback `button[aria-label*='Decline' i]` was also checked against this same live markup and matched nothing at all (the real reject aria-label contains no 'Decline' substring); left in the table since `#axeptio_btn_dismiss` already resolves reject via id and the dead fallback is inert, not harmful, but recorded here so a future pass does not assume it was verified live.

cmps.name: Civic Cookie Control
cmps.notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against https://cookiecontrol.com (Civic's own Cookie Control v9 deployment, loading cc.cdn.civiccomputing.com/9/cookieControl-9.x.min.js). The single most useful thing this capture established is that Cookie Control renders in two stages and half this table only exists in the second one: on first load the DOM has `#ccc` and `#ccc-overlay` plus the first-layer buttons `#ccc-notify-accept` ('I Accept') and `#ccc-notify-reject` ('I Do Not Accept'), while `#ccc-module`, `#ccc-close`, `#ccc-recommended-settings` ('Accept Recommended Settings') and `#ccc-reject-settings` ('I Do Not Accept') do not exist at all until the preferences panel is opened. `#ccc` alone carries the fingerprint and the container, so both still resolve at banner time. `settings` was the weak spot and gained a selector. `#ccc-icon` is real (aria-label 'Set cookie preferences.', confirmed live to open `#ccc-module`) but it is Cookie Control's optional persistent widget, and `#ccc-notify-button` matched nothing whatsoever on this capture. The actual first-layer settings launcher is a button with no id at all - `class='ccc-notify-button ccc-link ccc-tabbable ccc-notify-link'`, text 'Cookie Preferences' - so `.ccc-notify-link` was added (confirmed live: clicking it creates and shows `#ccc-module`). Without it, a deployment that turns the icon off would fingerprint as Civic and then report cmp_table_miss on `settings`, taking the whole settings -> toggles -> save denial path down with it. `#ccc-notify-button` is left in place: it is dead here rather than harmful, and it is recorded as unverified so a later pass does not mistake it for something this capture confirmed. `save` is `#ccc-close`, whose aria-label is plainly 'Close', and that is worth being precise about because it reads like a dismiss. It is not an accept control - the accept controls are the two ids above and it shares nothing with them - and clicking it live did persist: it rewrote `CookieControl` with a fresh consentDate. Cookie Control applies toggles immediately and writes consent as soon as the panel is touched, so a settings-path denial is genuinely recorded. But the two denial routes do not leave the same evidence, which matters to anything reading `consent_storage`: clicking `#ccc-notify-reject` wrote `optionalCookies:{'analytics':'revoked','marketing':'revoked'}`, whereas opening the panel and closing it with `#ccc-close` left `optionalCookies:{}` - the categories absent entirely rather than explicitly revoked. Only `interactedWith:true` separates that from a visitor who never chose, so a denial completed through the save fallback cannot be told apart from an untouched banner by category flags alone. `accept` was verified structurally only - by id, text and the `ccc-accept-button` class on both controls - and deliberately not clicked, so no capture here proves what it writes.
